discovery: Photonic crystals and photonic band gaps: controlling the propagation, emission and localization of light in periodic dielectric structures
subfield: Optics and photonics / wave physics in structured media
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can open a complete photonic band gap: Yablonovitch to suppress spontaneous emission, John to achieve strong localization of light near band edges and in disorder. Yablonovitch then realized the first three-dimensional full band gap (yablonovite, 1991). Joannopoulos turned the idea into a predictive science, using band-structure computation and design to engineer defect cavities, waveguides and omnidirectional reflectors. Together they showed that light obeys a solid-state physics of its own. This created an entire field: photonic-crystal fibres, high-Q nanocavities for cavity QED, slow light, integrated nanophotonics, and later topological photonics, which grew directly from photonic band structures. The concept reached well beyond optics, to phononic and acoustic crystals, metamaterials and matter-wave lattices. It is a rare case of deep conceptual originality producing a new discipline with lasting technological impact.
